Assets.NotesMarkdown: History shows Stop loss and Take profit by default, and the level that closed a trade is tinted, red for SL and green for TP, like MT5. An optional Reason column shows TP, SL, SO (stop-out), Manual, Partial or Close by. The order ticket's Sell and Buy buttons are tinted red and green, and the chart's 1-click buttons a little stronger. Tab counts show only on Trade and Pending. In By symbol view the group row says 2 positions, and Stop loss and Take profit show Custom when the positions differ (hover to see each). The order confirmation mentions max slippage only when you set a limit. A disabled Trade Assistant stays in place, dimmed. The right column fits Order ticket, Trade Assistant, Sessions and Account without cutting off the Account section. Charts keep candles above the time axis and scale to include the longest wicks. Margin level turns amber below your margin call level and red below stop-out; both levels are now in the account menu.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: Clicks answer at once: orders, closes and changes show Sending… immediately and finish in a fraction of a second, even on a slow computer, and live prices no longer slow the window down. Sign in inside the main window: it opens at its last size, and with Remember me it signs straight in. Choose Live or Demo when you sign in; a demo account under Live is refused with a clear message. Assets.NotesMarkdown: Position lines now work like MetaTrader. One setting, Settings > Chart > Position lines, replaces Position labels and Group labels at the same price: Each (the new default) draws a dotted line and a label for every position at its own price, however close they are, and never merges them into a "BUY x4" label; Grouped (average) draws one line per side at the lot-weighted average price, for example "BUY 0.05 @ 4173.90 avg · 5"; Off hides the entry lines. Click or hover always picks one position in Each, and the whole side in Grouped. Everyone who had Position labels on Grouped or All now starts on Each; Off stays Off.

The chart right-click menu has Chart settings, which opens Settings on its Chart page, and Show Bid/Ask line, the same choice as the new box in Settings > Chart. The position box you get by clicking a position line is smaller and matches the rest of the terminal: a BUY or SELL badge with a side-coloured edge, profit in green and loss in red, and the standard close button.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: Position, stop loss, take profit and pending order labels on the chart no longer smear into a solid patch when several prices are close together: every label is drawn on a thin, soft halo in the chart background colour of the current theme (dark or light), and all halos are drawn before all texts, so each label stays readable. The chart keeps hiding every bar in the weekend close and now also hides the flat bars of a symbol's closed hours using that symbol's own trading schedule: the Sunday reopen hour, the daily break, holidays and leftover flat rows no longer show as dead candles, while real bars and quiet bars in open hours are kept.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: The trade share card is redesigned. It is now just the card, centred over the dimmed terminal with rounded corners and a soft shadow, scaled to fit the window and never clipped, with three small round icons on its top-right corner: copy the trade text, save the PNG and close. A short note confirms a copy or a save, and Esc or a click outside the card closes it. The picture carries your broker's own look: its logo and colours (the logo and colour that come with your terminal, otherwise the ones your broker publishes), a large green or red profit or loss, the return on margin, entry, current or close price and the move in points, a small chart of the trade drawn from the real price history when it is available, the masked account and the date and time in your chosen time zone. The saved PNG is the card only.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: The lot size now follows your account's group. If your group has a larger minimum lot, a larger lot step or a smaller maximum than the symbol itself, the lots box starts at the group minimum instead of 0.01, is raised or lowered to the allowed range when you sign in, switch symbol or your broker changes the settings, and the minus and plus buttons move in the group's step and stop at its limits. While the lots are below the minimum, above the maximum or not on the step, Buy and Sell (and the one-click buttons) are switched off with a short reason under them, such as "Min 0.05 lots", "Max 2.00 lots" or "Lots in steps of 0.05", instead of failing after you click. Closing part of a position still uses the symbol's own step, so a partial close is not held to the group's larger step.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: The chart right-click menu is tidier: Show Ask line and the Position lines choices now use real check marks, so every label lines up with the items around it. Turning the Ask line off now hides only the Ask line; the current price line always stays on the chart (the same choice sits in Settings > Chart, worded the same). Updates are now your decision: when a new version has been downloaded the terminal shows "Update available" on the sign-in page and in the status bar, and installs it only when you click it (signed in, after a one-line confirm) or, if you never click, when you close the terminal yourself. It no longer restarts on its own and no longer closes a running terminal. A build your broker has retired shows an Update now button instead of restarting automatically.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: The chart right-click menu no longer shifts when you tick or untick Show Ask line: every label stays in place and only the tick appears or disappears. Settings now has a Check for updates button next to the version: it tells you whether you are on the latest version, offers an update with Update now when there is one, and never installs anything on its own. Switching to another account now fully loads that account's name, balance and positions (before, the new account number could show with the previous account's data). The Sign out confirmation is now one plain line: you'll need your password to sign in again.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: History now shows partial closes as soon as they happen. While a position is still open, each partial close is its own row in History (lots, close price, time and profit); once the position is fully closed, its closes are grouped into one row with the total lots, the average close price and the total profit, and you can expand it to see each close. A position closed in one go is a single row. The TODAY range now starts at the start of today in the time zone you chose in Settings (for Broker, the 17:00 New York rollover), and totals count each close on the day it happened. On the chart, when many positions or orders are outside the visible price range they no longer stack down the price scale: they show as one "N above" or "N below" marker, which lists them when you point at it and brings them into view when you click it.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: The account number box on the sign-in card now has a list of the accounts this computer has signed in to on this server, each with its server name. Pick one and its server is selected; if its sign-in is saved on this computer the password box is already filled, otherwise type the password. Accounts that are closed, removed or signed out of no longer appear. Before you sign in, the terminal now shows the Market Watch, the chart and the economic calendar as you last saw them, dimmed and marked "LAST KNOWN" with the time, instead of empty panels; your account, balance and positions stay hidden until you sign in, and everything turns live as soon as you do.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: History shows your period's full account figures: under the trade totals, deposits, withdrawals, credit, your initial balance, adjustments, the net change and the balance at the start and end of the range, the same figures your broker sees. A trade your broker voided stays in History, greyed and marked VOIDED, and is not counted in any total. The statement adds a cash-flow table, a summary and the opening and closing balance, lists each close under its position's ticket and shows voided trades on their own. Right-click a closed trade for Fill details.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: Placing, closing or modifying many positions at once no longer freezes the terminal: orders go out the moment you click, a burst of them leaves together, and the screen keeps moving while the answers come back. The terminal now shows your account plan (for example Standard or Pro) in the account header and in Account details, and never an internal group name. When the server refuses an order, a close or a modify, you now see one short plain message instead of technical text: Market closed, Off quotes - try again, Not enough margin, Invalid price, Invalid volume, Invalid SL or TP, Symbol not available, Trading disabled, Too many requests - wait a moment, Close already with the dealer, or Order rejected. In a bulk close or modify, each refused position shows its own message. When an order or close gets no answer at all, the terminal checks the server and shows the real result, or "No response - check your positions", and never sends it twice.

Assets.NotesMarkdown: Terminal 1.0.96: a cleaner, steadier terminal. Prices never go blank when the price feed drops: the last known prices stay, greyed, with "stale since HH:MM", and trading pauses until the feed is back (never a misleading "Off quotes"). The chart keeps its history with a marker where data is missing instead of jumping to an old price. New fonts (IBM Plex Sans for text, Plex Mono for figures), BUY in blue and SELL in red, a tidier Market Watch and tape. The Trade tab footer shows positions, lots per side, swap and commission; the chart shows one tag per side for each symbol ("7 SELL · 1.06"); the position menu is shorter; the fill details are shown inline instead of a popup. DAY P/L and WEEK P/L are now the server's realized figures for the trading day and week (closed trades with their swap and commission); open trades count only in OPEN P/L. If the figures cannot be read, the last ones stay greyed. A group row whose positions have different SL or TP levels is left empty instead of showing a dash. A position appears in the Trade tab only after the server confirms the fill (no more rows that show up and then vanish when an order is refused). Every refused order writes one line in LOG with the order, the reason code and the message (for example "REJECTED · SELL 0.01 XAUUSD MARKET @ 4019.92 · OFF_QUOTES · Off quotes - try again"). A market order waiting for the dealer shows in PENDING as AT DEALER, and leaves PENDING with its message if the dealer rejects it.

DAY P/L and WEEK P/L are now the server's realized figures for the trading day and week (closed trades with their swap and commission); open trades count only in OPEN P/L. If the figures cannot be read, the last ones stay greyed. A group row whose positions have different SL or TP levels is left empty instead of showing a dash. A position appears in the Trade tab only after the server confirms the fill (no more rows that show up and then vanish when an order is refused). Every refused order writes one line in LOG with the order, the reason code and the message (for example "REJECTED · SELL 0.01 XAUUSD MARKET @ 4019.92 · OFF_QUOTES · Off quotes - try again"). A market order waiting for the dealer shows in PENDING as AT DEALER, and leaves PENDING with its message if the dealer rejects it.

# Terminal 1.0.98

1. One logo everywhere: the gem, then QORE in the text colour and TRADER in gold. 14 px in the header, 20 px on sign-in, 11 px in the status bar. The square tile is only the Windows icon.
2. The THEME box now shows the theme you are in (dark shows DARK, light shows LIGHT). Click it to switch.
3. The status bar reads "QoreTrader · Live" with the dot after the text: green when connected, grey when offline.
4. The 1-CLICK chip is filled gold when it is ON and an outline when it is OFF.
5. SELL and BUY are solid blue and red buttons with white text and no border, in the chart strip, the order ticket and the close window. They get lighter on hover, darker when pressed, and fade to 40% when off.
6. The price on SELL and BUY keeps one colour. A small green or red arrow shows which way it moved.
7. Floating P/L in the footer has the same colour as Open P/L. BUY and SELL in the footer are coloured, and every cell has equal space on both sides with a thin divider.
8. In the 1-click strip the symbol has its own row above the buttons and the collapse arrow sits at the edge.
9. The small gold mark on top of the chart: we could not find it in our screens at 1920x1032 (single chart or 2x2). Send a screenshot if you still see it.
10. A disabled Trade assistant takes one row. RISK, REWARD and R:R appear once both SL and TP are set.
11. The arrow tool is the normal pointer; the crosshair appears only with the crosshair tool or while you draw.
12. Hold Ctrl to snap to candles while you draw. Let go and the magnet goes off.
13. The drawing toolbar sits at the top centre of the chart, you can drag it, it remembers its place and stays off the selected object. It has colour and opacity, width, line style, text, template, lock, clone, delete, settings and more.
14. While you draw, the line already looks as it will. End points are small circles. A hovered drawing lights up and shows a hand.
15. The Long and Short tools are two plain boxes (blue target side, red stop side) until you hover or select them; then you see handles, the Target and Stop texts, and the PnL, quantity and R:R chip.
16. Send to ticket passes the entry, stop, target and lots exactly as drawn: above the market it opens a Stop order, below it a Limit order, and close to the market a Market order. "Close" is the symbol's own minimum distance, or one spread when it has none.
17. Drawing settings have the tabs Style, Text, Coordinates and Visibility, a colour picker with opacity, Fibonacci level controls, templates and a live preview.
18. Position lines in "Each" are always one line per position. Labels are stacked when they overlap, up to 20 per side; any more become one "+N more" label. Lines are only grouped when you choose Grouped.
19. The chart header shows the time and open, high, low, close of the candle under the pointer, and goes back to the last candle when you move away. The floating readout is gone.
20. Switching to a 2x2 layout shows your drawings in every pane right away.
21. The order ticket opens on MARKET. A LIMIT or STOP tab starts at the middle of the spread with SL and TP empty, and follows when you change the symbol. On STOP both buttons stay off until you type a valid price, and the hint says which side is valid.
22. New ticket hint: "Price is below market → Buy Limit. To sell here use Sell Stop (STOP tab)."
23. Break-even now writes one line per position, "Break-even #… · SL → … · … ms", and one summary line only when there were several positions.
24. (Internal) A list of non-English characters in the code was prepared for review; nothing changed.

Assets.NotesMarkdown:
# Terminal 1.0.99

1. SELL and BUY have a soft glow at the top, a thin darker edge and rounded corners, in the chart strip, the order ticket and the close window. They get a little lighter on hover and darker when pressed. When a button cannot be used it turns into an outline with a light tint.
2. The small arrow on SELL and BUY is a plain white arrow with no dark box behind it. It is a little dimmer and lights up fully for a moment when the price moves.
3. Selected text, and the selected row in a list or drop-down, is blue in every box. The brand accent is no longer used for selection.
4. The start-up window shows the logo mark with the brand name in two colours: the first part in the text colour, the second in the brand accent.
5. When you are offline the bottom-left cell reads "QoreTrader · Offline" with a grey dot after the words.
6. A drawing you point at or select no longer gets a glowing band along the line. A selected drawing shows its end points and the toolbar; a drawing you point at gets only a slightly thicker line.
7. Drop-down lists, such as the account list on sign-in, close when you click anywhere outside, press Esc, or switch to another window.
8. With a drawing tool and the magnet on (or Ctrl held), the crosshair itself jumps to the nearest open, high, low or close of the candle under it, before you click and also for the first point.
9. The parallel channel works the way you draw it: two clicks for the first line, a third for the width. The second line is a copy of the first, the fill closes on the right corners, and you get a handle on each corner and in the middle of each line.
10. After the last click of a tool, moving the mouse no longer drags the chart. Esc stops any drag, and a missed button release is dropped.
11. Drawings and their labels are cut off at the edge of the chart and no longer paint over the price scale or the time scale.
12. We could not find the large empty blue rectangle on our screens. The selection box of a drawing is now checked to stay the size of the drawing. Send a screenshot if you still see it.
13. RISK % stays empty until a stop loss is set, and the hint about the smallest lot only appears when there is a stop loss and it is true. Changing the symbol clears both.
14. The History footer shows BALANCE (the closing balance only), DEPOSITS, WITHDRAWALS and PROFIT. It shows OPENING only when your period starts after the account was opened, and "OPENED 16 Oct" when the account was opened inside the period.
15. Click a History column header to sort by it: once for ascending, again for descending, a third time for the default (newest on top). The choice is remembered for each account.
16. The new sound set is in. Settings > Notifications now has one Sounds switch and a volume slider; the per-event boxes, PLAY buttons and price-feed switches are gone.
17. Max slippage is gone from Settings, the order ticket and the New order window, and the terminal no longer sends a slippage limit with an order. Your broker's own limit is the only one.
18. Position tags on the chart now use colour for meaning: BUY is blue and SELL is red, and the profit or loss figure is blue for a profit and red for a loss. The lot size and the close cross stay in the normal text colour.
19. On the chart, the line between a position's price and its profit or loss now has proper spacing ("4444.00 · 7.25 USD") instead of running together.
20. The LIMIT and STOP price now follows the market until you type your own; the refresh arrow next to it brings it back. The two hint paragraphs are gone: only the side that does not fit the price is switched off.
21. On the STOP tab the price follows the ask plus your symbol's minimum distance (one point if there is none), so Buy Stop is ready at once. On the LIMIT tab it follows the middle of the spread, or a little below the bid when the minimum distance is wider than the spread.
22. Tooltips now open already finished: the panel colour, border, font and full text are there from the first frame, with no dark box or odd symbols, and a tooltip with no text never opens.
23. Chart toolbar tooltips are plain text in the terminal font, with no special symbols.
24. A one-minute candle that was skipped on the chart is now filled in again, including after the connection comes back.
25. The chart's 1-click strip keeps its familiar layout: SELL, the lot box and BUY in one row, the 1-CLICK switch under them on the left, and no margin line under the buttons (a button that cannot be used still says why when you point at it).
26. The order ticket shows RISK, REWARD and R:R under SELL and BUY at all times; they stay empty until a stop loss and a take profit are set.
27. The Trade assistant is always fully shown. When it is off, its text and fields are greyed and the ENABLE switch looks normal.
28. On the chart, the cross at the end of a position's tag closes that position through the usual confirmation (no confirmation if you turned Confirmations off). Clicking the tag itself only selects that position's row in Positions. The small pop-up window that used to open is gone.
29. The minimise, maximise and close buttons of the window show a clear hover state, with no tooltips.
30. If QoreTrader closed unexpectedly, the next start says so in one line, "The app closed unexpectedly. Report saved.", with an Open folder link. Every window close is now written to the log with who asked for it.
